idiom_name: Prisma cursor + take with an opaque boundary token
implementation_notes: Prisma exposes cursor pagination as query options: .cursor(...) must follow .orderBy(...), .take(n) returns the records after (or, with a negative take, before) the cursor record, and .skip(1) drops that record itself - the docs require the cursor to be a unique, sequential column and to be passed a value for every field you sorted by. The boundary still owns the opaque token (base64url or encrypted JSON of the cursor fields) and the pinned filter; the classical hand-written cursor codec is only needed when the store is not Prisma, and then the emitted SQL should still be the same keyset predicate.
pitfalls: Passing only the id while ordering by (createdAt, id) misplaces the cursor: Prisma requires a value for every sorted field, and the cursor column must be unique and sequential.
Mixing .skip() with .cursor() beyond skip: 1 is offset pagination in disguise - pages drift under writes - and cursor pagination cannot jump to a numbered page or count rows.
